findings.title: Cleanup interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The global cleanup ticker is changed from time.Minute * 10 to time.Minute * 1. This is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix and runs every cleanup job (expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) ten times as often, significantly increasing database and CPU load. If a full cleanup pass takes longer than one minute, the ticker can also cause back-to-back cleanup passes. This looks like an accidental debug change and should be reverted or explicitly justified before merging.

findings.title: Cleanup logs at Error level with full ID lists on every batch
findings.body: The new cleanup path calls r.log.Error for 'Annotations to clean by time/count', 'cleaned annotations by ...', 'Tags to clean', and 'cleaned tags' on every batch, passing the complete 'ids' slice. With a batch size such as the newly tested 32767, every successful cleanup cycle emits multiple error-level log records containing tens of thousands of IDs. This creates noisy error logs, can make error monitoring misleading, and can produce very large log payloads. These are normal debug/info events, not errors, and the full ID lists should not be logged at this level.

findings.title: DELETE placeholders can exceed database parameter limits except on SQLite
findings.body: deleteByIDs only special-cases SQLite when building the DELETE statement with an IN clause. For other supported databases with parameter limits, such as SQL Server (2100 parameters) and depending on batch size PostgreSQL, setting AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above that limit will generate DELETE FROM ... WHERE id IN (?,?,...) with too many bind parameters and fail. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not bind one parameter per ID. The ID list should be batched for deletion across all dialects, or equivalent dialect-specific limits should be applied.
